history.outcome: Failed on two checks, but isolated the cause. Ordered before any face-ability change, the ruler left its natural spawn point (cached island 2 == fresh island 2) and reached the other landmass. After the wall toggles, every sampled AI party held a cached island 2 while fresh lookups returned 4. The player then could not walk back after the wall was re-enabled (same stale cache). The AI return trip timed out because the stall detector counted an in-progress embark transition as a stall.

criteria.c2:
Met in both worlds. The barrier evidence:
- Default finds no path to the other landmass, while All does with 2 transitions. The landmass is separated from town_1's by water alone; the builder checks that all non-water cells form different components.
- Port-to-port engine sea routes stay on sea faces where the straight line crosses land (both worlds). Actual ship movement around land: world 43's player voyage (427.3 traveled vs 303.5 straight line, all samples at sea) and world 42's voyage in run 28652. In world 42 of the accepted run, the actual crossings to the nearest landmass are short and straight, and their straight lines touch no land.
- Naval cannot reach the land-enclosed lake, while All reaches it from its own shore (positive control, 1 transition).
- The land route past the lake goes around it.
- Disabling face group 5 (the seed-derived wall) changes the actual engine route: open 89.8/81.3 crossing the wall in 51/40 samples; closed 105.0/86.9 with 0 wall samples. The toggle hits exactly 2 faces per wall cell (16/20).
- The player's planned path changed, and the player walked around the closed wall (104.4/86.4 traveled, 0 wall samples) and back through it once reopened (22/18 wall samples).
The open-sea (Default) and inland-gate (Naval) refusals are sanity checks only, because their destination faces are themselves invalid for those types.

knownGaps: Stale face caches after face-ability changes. Scene.SetAbilityOfFacesWithId renumbers navigation islands (2 -> 4). Every party whose stored CampaignVec2 cached a face beforehand stops moving: MobileParty's move step compares the current face island with the next position's island. The IL reading is supported by runs 17804, 21284 and 22588 rather than confirmed independently. The probe's compensation (RefreshFaceCaches) rebuilds only MobileParty CampaignVec2 fields; settlement gate/port positions and other cached positions are not refreshed. Any runtime obstruction feature needs a supported, complete equivalent; a follow-up was raised.
No bridges. The generated terrain authors no bridge (17) or UnderBridge (25) faces, so ships under or around a bridge are unmet.
No stitching. There is no runtime navmesh prefab assembly or stitching for campaign worlds.

The obstruction change is a runtime toggle of the builder-stamped, seed-derived wall. Two different seeds give different wall positions, but a single world regenerated with a changed obstruction was not run as a separate pair.
The AI is ordered by script (SetDoNotMakeNewDecisions + SetMoveGoToPoint(All)). AI parties choosing ships on their own was not observed, although caravans and naval patrols were at sea.

Reverse-direction party movement: the player reversed on land and the AI reversed across the sea. The player did not sail back. In world 42 the off-shore landmass has no port to set sail from; in world 43 town_2 has a port, but a return voyage was not run.
The world 43 cross-landmass routes are asymmetric in the engine (e.g. Naval port-to-port 426.2 vs 438.0). Both directions are found with 2 transitions where expected.

Route classification samples segments every 0.25 units through land and sea face lookups; coastal samples are classified by those lookups. Water rendering is shown only by engine screenshots (ships and parties on rendered water and shore), not measured.
limitations: Two seed worlds, one process, fast-forward time.
The embark time comes from NavalDLCPartyTransitionModel: 0-3 h observed with a valid anchor; 48 h without one per IL, not observed.
reviewNotes: Independent read-only re-review of run 2248: c1 PASS-WITH-CAVEATS, c2 PASS-WITH-CAVEATS, c3 PASS, no blocking defects. Its wording fixes are applied.

Open code nits, deliberately not changed so the probe source hash stays that of the accepted run:
(a) Travel's arrival check runs before the transition-wait update, so the last wait can stay open:true (world 43 player disembark).
(b) World 43's AI has two disembark waits 0.00075 days apart; the restart is unexplained.
(c) stateAtSpawn/faceCacheAtSpawn are recorded after the conditional LeaveSettlementAction, which did not fire.
(d) The 2000-point track cap truncates world 43's voyage track (2412 samples).
